description: Claim an in-world object as 'mine'. Prerequisite: none — the object must exist in the current lot but no ownership verification is performed by the engine; this is a sidecar-side intention marker. Effect: the sidecar writes a claim record to the persona's persistent state directory so the claim survives sidecar and session restarts. The claim appears in the next perception tick as body.my_objects[]. A second claim on the same object_id updates the note and timestamp (last-writer-wins). Cost: none in real seconds or motives. NOT a FreeSO wire action — this is a sidecar-only affordance and is invisible to other Sims unless you choose to speak about it. Use query-claims to list what you currently claim.

args.name: target_object_id
args.description: The numeric object_id of the thing to claim. Obtain this from query-nearby or query-inventory. Must be a positive integer.

args.name: note
args.description: Optional short note about why you are claiming this object (e.g. 'my bed', 'the fridge I stocked'). Stored verbatim and returned by query-claims. Keep it brief — one clause.

common_mistakes: Passing target_object_id as 0 — rejected with ok:false. Use a real object_id from query-nearby.
Treating a claim as engine-enforced ownership — it is not. Other Sims can still interact with the object. The claim is your internal affordance marker, not a lock.
Forgetting that claims survive sidecar restart but are per-persona — another Sim's sidecar does not see your claims.
refuse_conditions: missing or zero target_object_id → ok:false with 'target_object_id is required and must be positive'
